title: Participant API (v0.4)
description: The only window a controller has onto the world. Identical for code, LLM, human and RL controllers (VISION principle 4). Shaped like PettingZoo's AEC API: the environment selects the next participant to act (the one whose wake time or triggering event comes first on the world clock), the participant reads last() and calls step(action). There are no turns. A participant perceives only through its channels; there is no mandate and no approval queue in v0.2, because authority is a matter of records and people (D20).

StepResult.description: What last() returns for the selected participant. 'reward' is always 0: the platform does not judge. Researchers who want RL rewards compute them outside the world from logs or observations and wrap the environment.

termination.description: The participant has opted out of the study (VISION §15; D38) and no stand-in continues it.

truncation.description: The run reached clock.run_seconds or was stopped.

Observation.description: What a participant perceives. Built by the kernel (deterministic, logged by hash) plus 'drafts' and 'notices', added by the orchestrator. 'outcomes', 'inbox' and 'notices' hold only what is new since the participant's previous observation.

entity.description: A person's participant: its person (it acts as this person). Absent for a system.

body.description: A person's participant: its own body, in full (it always knows its age, whether it's in the world, and what's wrong with it).

treated.description: Care has been given for it.

sex.description: Biological sex, where the world models it.

children.description: Its children, as a parent knows them.

sex.description: Biological sex, where the world models it.

variables.description: Its variables (the world's body_variables), as they are now.

in.description: The space it's in (a body is in one at a time), if any.

positions.description: The positions it holds now. Their channels are in 'channels' as '<position>/<channel>'.

notices.description: Added by the orchestrator: what the participant needs to know about its own requests that isn't world state, e.g. that a proposal couldn't be drafted, or that a draft it tried to sign doesn't exist. Logged as annotations (translation_failure, note). Absent when there are none.

re.description: The draft or proposal it's about.

readings.description: Readings of records this participant can see, by record id (docs/design/rebuild.md section 7).

woke_for.description: Why this wake: the time it asked for, its cadence, news (a message, a record naming it), or an act of its own finished.

since.description: World seconds since this unit's previous wake (0 at its first): flows are computed from it, never per wake (docs/design/rebuild.md 6.5).

Outcome.description: What happened to one of this participant's actions. There are only two outcomes: applied, or refused because it was physically impossible.

surveyed.description: A survey's estimates (nature), for the one who surveyed only: what of, and each cell's estimate.

investigated.description: What an investigation found, for the one who investigated only: whether goods were taken as said, and the taker if found (null: not found).

seen.description: Work done on buildings by people sent to them (those doing it were there): each building worked on, as they left it, for the one whose work it was. How a crew knows what it left behind without anyone being shown the town. Work nobody is named as doing shows nothing.

as.description: The position it wrote in (absent: as itself).

from_entity.description: Who acted in writing it: the person, or the organisation acted for through a position (docs/design/rebuild.md 7.4).

LookRequest.description: Look through one of the participant's channels now (attention). On-request channels are perceived only this way. A look through a records channel may carry a query: a search, which returns what matches now rather than what changed; through a register asked of its keeper (`way: ask`) it must, and the query must name its subject (`field = value` on one of the channel's `by` fields); through a board it must, within the board's `most`. A look through a directory must say whom (`who`). A look through a map of places gone to (`way: visit`) must say where (`visit`): it takes the looker's time, and what it finds arrives when it ends.

who.description: A look-up in a directory: exactly one of an entity (alone: its entry; with `role`: that organisation's positions of that role), a participant (the person it acts as), a position, or a name (the entities of exactly that name or id, the positions of exactly that title, role or id, and the person a participant of that id acts as; capitals aside). At most 20 entries to a look-up, in id order. Several look-ups through the same directory in one look are answered together.

visit.description: Going to look: the places gone to, in order (a building, or a cell of ground). The looker is busy for the way there and back and the world's time to look at each place; what was there then comes with the observation after.

Query.description: A search over records: mechanical matching on named fields, never interpretation.

standing.description: Only records still standing: not withdrawn by their own author (or whoever they speak for). Withdrawals themselves never stand.

QueryField.description: A place in a record: id (the record's own), record (its kind of record), kind (a statement's kind), at, author, speaks_for, basis, claim (the claim a transfer or a release names), holder (who holds a claim), data.<path> (a statement's data) or about.<path> (a claim's contents). Where the place holds a list, `=` holds if the list has the value and `!=` if it does not (a plan's cells: which lot a cell is on).

version.description: Translator release; prompt changes bump it so experiments can hold it fixed.

Draft.description: A plain-language proposal as the participant will see it before anything takes effect: the translator's call, the resolver's acts, and a mechanical preview of exactly what will happen, in world terms. draft_hash = SHA-256 of 'oikos.draft.v1\n' + canonical JSON of this object. The confirmed hash is carried into the act command, so the participant confirmed exactly this.

as.description: The capacity the acts are made in: a position it holds (absent: as itself).

call.description: The translator's reading of the proposal, in the call language (canonical form).

summary.description: The preview: exactly what the blocks will do, generated mechanically from them in world terms (never written by the translator).

check.description: Kernel dry run of the blocks at drafting time: would physics allow them? Plus the translator's warnings about records (e.g. laws the plan appears to break). The world may change before sign-off; the kernel re-checks on submission.

warnings.description: Things the translator noticed but the kernel doesn't judge, e.g. 'this appears to break law rec.4 (river zone)'. Informational; the participant decides.

caveats.description: Parts of the proposal the translator could not express in blocks.

ChannelData.description: What a look through a channel delivers: what changed within its scope since the participant's previous look through it (a first look: everything it covers). Accounts: accounts opened, whose balance moved, or closed ('closed'); transactions since the previous look. Records: new records. Sites: cells whose building, or whose building's occupants, changed. Directory: new entities, and positions created or handed over. A channel that isn't due (its 'every') is absent.

closed.description: The account was closed since the participant's previous look.

transactions.description: Transfers touching these accounts since the participant's previous look through an accounts channel.

holdings.description: Holdings of the participant's entity that changed since its previous look (a first look: all it holds, nothing at 0). A quantity of 0: all gone from there.

search.description: These are a search's results (what matches now), not what's new since the last look.

whole.description: The participant's entity has moved since its last look through this channel (which looks near it): these are everything the channel now covers, in place of what it covered before.

as_of.description: When this view was last refreshed (see the channel's 'every').

whole.description: The capacity's entity has moved since its last look through this channel (which looks near it): these cells are the whole of its new surroundings, in place of the old.

visited.description: This is what a visit found: the places gone to, as they were at `as_of` (the participant's memory of them, not a standing view).

seen.description: Nature: conspicuous species anyone there would notice (never how many).

participant.description: A person's participant (who acts as them).

positions.description: Organisations' positions, and who holds them now: the participant, and a name (the person's, or a system's title).

oneOf.description: The entity's own record (world-config Channel kind own_record): present when it has changed since the previous look, and in a first look where there is one. Its sections are the mind's (a person's: entity-record.schema.json).

ParticipantAction.description: What a participant passes to step(). Carries no participant id: the orchestrator binds identity from the connection. act and message go straight to the kernel; call (a structured intent in the call language) goes to the resolver, which turns it into the participant's own acts; propose (plain language) goes to the translator and resolver and comes back as a draft to confirm; sign confirms (accept) or declines (reject) a draft; wait yields until 'until' or the next item addressed to this participant, whichever is first; opt_out leaves the study (VISION §15; D38): always available and final. It is not resigning an office, which is an ordinary act in the world.

as.description: The position to act in (absent: as itself, a person's only).

by.description: Who does the act's work, if not the actor alone (foundations F3): people at work, whose time it takes.

call.description: An intent in the call language (contracts/calls.md), e.g. money(to=builder, amount="$500"). The resolver turns it into the participant's own acts (docs/design/translator-and-resolver.md).

as.description: The position to act in (absent: as itself, a person's only).
The position to act in (absent: as itself, a person's only).
The position to act in (absent: as itself, a person's only).

Reading.description: The platform's mechanical reading of a record by its own terms (docs/design/rebuild.md section 7): beside the record, never in its place, and it changes nothing by itself. A participant may read the records differently.

SiteStructure.description: The building standing on this cell (the same on every cell of its footprint).

variables.description: Its state variables (phase B), each as a value on a day with its rate now and bounds: today's value is value + per_day x (days since), within bounds.

count.description: How many bodies are in it.

occupants.description: Who, where that can be told: in the capacity's own buildings, or through a channel that shows names. Absent: only how many.

left.description: Its last few departures (who left, why, when), where the channel shows who's there: those who share it see someone move out, be removed or die.

seen_leaving.description: From outside (where who is there can't be told): when someone was last seen leaving this space (moving out, being put out, going from the world), of its last few departures. Never who; a death inside is not seen from outside, so a home that has emptied with nobody seen leaving is one a neighbour may wonder about.

seen_entering.description: From outside: when someone was last seen going into this space. Never who. Someone seen going in after anyone was last seen leaving, in a space with nobody in it now, has not come out.
